headline: Barbados and the UN will co-host a Special Summit on AI Safety on 23 November, as UNIDIR examined armed violence in Africa and orbital data centre sovereignty, and a retrospective found the feared 'Black October' AI-cyberattack wave never materialized.

points.text: Barbados and the United Nations announced they will co-host a Special Summit on AI Safety on 23 November, bringing together governments, tech companies, scientists and civil society.
UNIDIR, Switzerland, and the UN Regional Centre for Peace and Disarmament in Africa launched a new phase of the Lomé Initiative to break the cycle of armed violence in Africa.
UNIDIR examined the sovereignty question raised by orbital data centres, as demand for data storage and processing pushes into space.
A newsletter made the case for building 'Eurofab' to close Europe's chip gap.
Axios reported that the feared wave of automated attacks exploiting the AI-discovered 'Black October' web vulnerabilities has struggled to get off the ground, delivering a Y2K-like lesson.
The ITU's AI for Good initiative highlighted work on building the foundations for AI infrastructure and trust.
Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model it says marks a significant leap for cybersecurity and cyber defense, with initial access limited to vetted defenders.
